name: native-local-owners-and-forge-selection
reason: Replace VM owners with one configured native task owner and owned worktree per PR. Retain ownership, scope and stack variant boundaries.
anchor: 2. **Spawn one owner per PR, and keep its work where a replacement can find it.** Resolve the forge once for the program. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, use `origin pr` for every PR operation. Otherwise stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Never require Graphite (`gt`). Each owner is a Cursor cloud agent that builds, opens its PR per `playbooks/opening-a-pr.md`, proves the change on the real artifact, babysits to green per `playbooks/babysit.md`, and merges once steps 4 and 5 clear it. Where that playbook says to report a rebase, the owner rebases its own branch and publishes it with `git push --force-with-lease`.

name: use-delivered-pre-commit-review
reason: Use the bundled review skills rather than Cursor plugin commands.
anchor: Open the PR early so CI and bots run alongside the work. The code is ready only after the slop-strip (the `deslop` skill from the `cursor-team-kit` plugin (`/deslop`)) and the `/no-comments` pass, so the full swarm runs on finished code. Then rebase onto current trunk and report the code-ready head before self-proof, so verification runs on the base the patch lands on. Report every later head, and merge-ready once self-proof, CI, and babysit are done. Fix rounds stay on that base unless trunk conflicts, breaks CI, or lands a known concurrent change to the same files, because each rebase restarts CI. Run the repo's checks for the touched paths on the committed head before the code-ready push and before a later push that needs a verifier.

name: checkpoint-local-owned-work
reason: Replace transient VM/store assumptions with auditable local trails and explicit pickup, preserving the lease and ownership discipline.
anchor: Assume the VM dies. Soon after starting, push and start a decision trail in the root agent's store (path in the system prompt) per the **show-me-your-work** skill, then push each finished unit before you start the next. Whoever spawns a subagent records its id, state, and a stuck-after runtime from past runs of its kind in that store, so the root can probe it if the parent dies. Force-push only your own branch, with `--force-with-lease` pinned to the SHA you last pushed or took over, and on any push you did not make, stop and report to the root.

Record each task ID, worktree, branch, last pushed SHA, state and stuck-after runtime in the trail so a fresh owner can pick it up explicitly. name: use-native-swarm-for-proof
reason: Keep independent live proof with the delivered local workflow.
anchor: 4. **Swarm-verify once.** A full swarm runs once, at the code-ready head. Another full swarm runs only for new behavior, a redesign, or a large new diff. A rebase, a merge-conflict resolution, or a minor fix gets a single verifier at the new head, and a wording-only change gets none. Fan out independent verifiers at the code-ready SHA per the **swarm** skill. They re-run the gates, prove the load-bearing behavior live on the real surface through its control skill (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit`) or a named driver, and audit the diff. The verdict is not clean without the live lane, or before you audit the merge-ready report's receipts, because no lane trusts a claim it has not checked.
find: Fan out independent verifiers at the code-ready SHA per the **swarm** skill.
replace: Fan out independent non-author verifiers at the code-ready SHA using [swarm](../../swarm/SKILL.md).

name: audit-only-during-the-live-run
reason: Replace Cursor recurring loops with explicit root audits using actual task outcomes and owned side effects; checkpoint rather than promising takeover.
anchor: On the operator's go, arm `/loop 1h` to audit until no delegated work is left, because long runs drift and agents stall silently. Each tick re-reads this playbook from trunk and fixes drift, such as an unreported head or an unrecorded agent, by having its owner record it, because drift is a gap in the record, not a stall. It probes every agent, down to the leaf lanes, and judges each by its side effects, because status text and summaries can hide a stuck child. An agent is stuck when it errors, cannot start turns, or shows nothing new past its stuck-after runtime, and so is an owner that has neither pushed nor written a trail row by the first tick. One waiting on you or the operator is not stuck, so answer it. Replace a stuck agent at once, without waiting for its stop to land. A tick that changed something for the operator ends by catching them up per the **ketchup** skill, and one that changed nothing stays quiet.
replace: On the operator’s go, regularly audit the live run until no delegated work is left, using the bounded waits in [Autonomous run](autonomous-run.md). Re-read the active playbook on each audit, including the stack variant when selected. Check task outcomes and the owned branches and trails down to the leaf lanes; status text alone does not prove progress. A task that cannot run, errors or shows no new effect past its recorded stuck-after runtime needs replacement; waiting for a real gate is not a stall. Stop the old owner or verify its checkout is quiescent before another owner writes there. Give a fresh owner the exact recorded state and verify it before continuing. When an audit changes the operator’s outcome, [catch them up](../../ketchup/SKILL.md). If the session ends, hand off; no task or schedule is promised to survive.
